Evidence shows clear target engagement with comprehension scores >60% across all groups, demonstrating the intervention successfully delivered and was understood by participants. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The proposed mechanism is structured risk communication leading to cognitive processing and emotional regulation. The trial shows successful pathway modulation with high comprehension scores (82.4-94.6%) and manageable distress levels (4-5.25 on IGT-AD scale), indicating the intervention achieved its intended psychological and cognitive effects. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Both primary endpoints were met successfully. Comprehension scores exceeded the 60% threshold across all groups, and psychological distress remained at acceptable levels 6 weeks post-disclosure. This demonstrates successful clinical translation of the intervention's mechanism. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The trial revealed differential responses between subgroups - amyloid-positive participants had lower comprehension scores than amyloid-negative participants, and their co-participants showed higher distress. However, both subgroups still achieved successful outcomes above the predefined thresholds. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a small single-arm study (N=20) with no control group, which limits the strength of conclusions. However, the intervention had clear pre-specified success criteria that were met, and the behavioral nature of the intervention makes placebo effects less concerning than in drug trials.
